title: Article 3.5 amendment (OPAG-474): stage the root launcher as X-rc.N, publish final X straight to latest after qualification
description: HELD: do not start implementation until opum-doc's amendment to constitution Article 3.5 (and the staged-paired-release ADR it restates) is ratified by the operator first-party (Article 2.3). The ODOC id will follow from opum-agent; record it here when it arrives, and read the ratified text in opum-doc rather than a relay of it. Why: OPAG-474. npm's package-level readme for @opum-ai/lore is 0 bytes. Measured here 2026-09-27 by full packument read (registry.npmjs.org): top-level readme length 0 and readmeFilename empty; versions 0.6.2..0.9.3 carry NO readmeFilename key (published by tarball-file publish with npm 12.0.2, straight to latest), while 0.11.0 (npm 12.1.0, staged under release-candidate, latest moved by dist-tag) is the first to record readmeFilename README.md, and a dist-tag move does not copy it to the top level. So npm has likely never shown lore's README; staging did not remove it. Under Article 3.5 as written nothing is ever published onto latest, so no remedy exists without the amendment. Operator ruling (first-party, orchestrator session b8ab1ed4, 2026-09-27T18:45:19Z, as recorded on OPAG-474): the ROOT LAUNCHER @opum-ai/lore stages as X-rc.N under release-candidate and opum-cli-e2e qualifies it; the final X is then published straight to latest, after quest. The six platform packages stage and promote by dist-tag exactly as today. The qualified and shipped launchers must differ only by the version string, enforced in CI. Design note for implementation: the launcher tarball is package.json, README.md, LICENSE, bin/. The version appears in package.json and in README.md inside the lore-version managed blocks (published-bullet, status), so the diff check has to decide how README's version mentions are compared (for example: substitute X-rc.N -> X in every file of the qualified tarball, then require byte-identity with the shipped tarball, which also catches a status line that reads differently for an rc). Supersedes the README/checklist placement halves of LCLI-616 and LCLI-618, which now follow the final latest publish rather than a dist-tag move.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The amendment is ratified in opum-doc and its ODOC id and ratified text (read in opum-doc, by ref) are recorded on this task before any implementation starts

Staging publishes the root launcher @opum-ai/lore as X-rc.N under release-candidate, whose optionalDependencies pin the six platform packages at exactly X; the platform packages stage as X under release-candidate as today; both publish-release.sh and release.yml do this, and tests pin it

The final step publishes @opum-ai/lore X straight to latest only after the pair receipt for the staged pair verifies, and only after quest (Article 3 ordering), and moves the platform packages latest by dist-tag as today; no path publishes a launcher onto latest without that receipt

CI mechanically refuses a shipped X launcher tarball that differs from the qualified X-rc.N tarball in anything but the version string, with the README version handling decided and written down; a mutant with a non-version diff is shown red and a version-only diff green
The pair-receipt reader (scripts/pair-receipt.mjs) reads what opum-cli-e2e writes for an rc launcher, confirmed with opum-cli-e2e and quest-cli
After the final publish, npm view @opum-ai/lore readme is non-empty, measured by byte count with the command recorded (OPAG-474 AC3); the runbook states the new flow
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers every release.yml and scripts/ change

plan: P1 numbering: launcher stages as X-rc.N, N from 1, re-stage takes N+1; package.json on main stays X so Article 3.6 parity is unchanged
P2 rc launcher optionalDependencies pin the six platforms at exactly X; platforms stage as X under release-candidate as today
P3 README managed version blocks rendered for final X before staging, so X-rc.N -> X is a no-op on README (ADR Amendment 1 option 1)
P4 release.yml package job builds rc and final launchers from one source; CI asserts per-file (unpacked trees) that rc with X-rc.N -> X equals final, no missing or extra file

P5 promote: receipt verifies -> re-run P4 equivalence against the registry-served rc tarball (integrity per receipt) vs the X tarball -> platform latest by dist-tag -> publish launcher X --tag latest, last, quest before lore; rollback restores moved tags

P6 receipt shape is opum-cli-e2e's: proposed pair.

.version = X, launcher key opum-ai-

-X-rc.N.tgz, new pair.

.launcherVersion; pair-receipt.mjs follows whatever they settle
Pairing: P1-P6 sent to quest-cli (QCLI-399) and P6 to opum-cli-e2e 2026-09-27; implementation waits for their answers

NEXT (next session): fix review findings 1, 2, 4, 5 on this branch (reviewer pass on the fix); then PART B: pair-receipt.mjs reads launcherVersion + launcher tarball per opum-cli-e2e receipts/README.md steps 5-7 (merge 4f078e6b); promote-latest.mjs takes the Release run, checks the X tarball sha256 against launcherSubstitution.finalTarball, re-runs the equivalence against the registry-served rc, moves platforms latest by dist-tag, publishes the X launcher --tag latest last (after quest), verifies all seven and that latest serves X, rollback restores tags; the release-candidate tag test admits exactly that one publish in the promote script; README packument read-back non-empty (OPAG-474 AC3, with LCLI-616). Then mark PR #337 ready, gates, reviewer, land, promote.
implementationNotes: ORCHESTRATOR RULING on the README design point (opum-agent, cross-session, 2026-09-27, sent to opum-doc for the amendment text): 'differ only by the version string' means substituting X-rc.N with X throughout the rc launcher yields the final launcher byte for byte. So the README status block (lore-version managed blocks) must be rendered so that this holds -- e.g. rendered for the final X before staging, or carrying only the version token. If that proves unworkable, argue it on this task with specifics and opum-agent will revisit. This is a relay of the orchestrator's design ruling; the binding text is the ratified amendment in opum-doc (AC1).

The root launcher (@opum-ai/lore: package.json, README.md, LICENSE, bin/) stages as prerelease X-rc.N under release-candidate, is qualified by opum-cli-e2e, and reaches latest by a FRESH PUBLISH of X, never a dist-tag move. 'The qualified X-rc.N and the published X must be identical once X-rc.N is substituted for X throughout, checked mechanically in CI: the version string is the only permitted difference, including inside any managed block the launcher's own README carries, such as a status line naming the release.' Rollback stays dist-tag based, the launcher's own latest included: restore every moved tag to its recorded prior value, retry at the same version, never skip to a different number; nothing is unpublished or overwritten. ADR Amendment 1 adds: render the README status block for the final X before staging, or carry only a version token substituted at both stages. Quest publishes its launcher to latest before Lore's. PAIRED DESIGN SETTLED with quest-cli (QCLI-399), 2026-09-27, cross-session, both sides agreeing P1-P6 with these refinements: (i) P3 REPLACED -- the rc launcher README renders the launcher's OWN version X-rc.N in its lore-version managed blocks, so X-rc.N -> X carries it to X; chosen because LCLI-510's shipped-README assertion checks each packed tarball's README against that tarball's own package.json version and so holds unmodified for both launchers. (ii) P4 equivalence is ENTRY BY ENTRY over the unpacked tarballs: same set of paths (none missing, none extra), each entry's mode equal, each content byte-identical after replacing every X-rc.N with X; never whole tar/gzip bytes. (iii) P5 order is fixed: receipt verifies -> equivalence re-check of the registry-served rc launcher (integrity per receipt) against the X launcher from the SAME Release run, whose digest is checked first -> platforms latest by dist-tag -> npm publish X launcher --tag latest, last, quest before lore -> verify all seven; rollback restores every latest by dist-tag, the launcher's included. (iv) The release-candidate tag test admits exactly ONE publish without --tag release-candidate: the X launcher with --tag latest, in the promote script only. (v) Eight tarballs in the Release run's npm-packages artifact (platforms @X, launcher @X-rc.N pinning platforms at exactly X, launcher @X); seven staged; the X launcher is never staged. P6 (receipt shape) is opum-cli-e2e's to rule; readers wait for it.
